_doc: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the G1 Newton walk train<->deploy physical model.
Both the GPU trainer (projects/policies/research/training/gpu_newton_g1_walk_trainer.py) and
the OmniSim deploy (the embedded-Python Newton backend, driven via the
OMNISIM_NEWTON_* env vars emitted by scripts/dev/g1_deploy_launch.py) derive
their physics model from THIS file + the prim URDF. Nothing here may be
re-declared as a literal constant on either side -- import g1_physics_spec
instead. The geometry / inertia / per-joint position+velocity+effort limits
are NOT duplicated here: they are read live from the prim URDF by the loader.
Every value below equals the WINNING walker's value
(runs/gpu_newton_g1_walk_ft_pdoff_clamp, 5.9 m / 33.8 s). Changing a value
here changes the physics for BOTH sides -- retrain + redeploy to validate.
Known trainer<->deploy residuals that are NOT yet unified are listed under
'_residuals' so they are explicit, not silent.
DETERMINISTIC OPEN-LOOP PHYSICS PROBE (no RL) for binary-level trainer<->deploy
parity certification. The SAME scripted joint-target sequence is applied in the
trainer Python solver (build_g1_native-style) AND in the deploy binary (the
humanoid_stand_deploy controller in omnisim-bin), and the resulting per-tick
trajectories are diffed. This is the FIRST test that steps the real binary, not the
g1_deploy_runtime.py extract. Probe the model + stepping, NOT balance/durability.
static_base welds the floating base (staticBase) so the inverted-pendulum chaos
cannot confound a real physics gap with chaotic amplification -- that is the
chaos-free numerical-equality lane. Free the base (static_base=false) for the
realistic lane. 'hold' = freeze every joint at pose; 'sinusoid' = a deterministic
per-joint sweep (the most sensitive probe). ke/kd default to the deterministic
STAND gains (a stiff position-PD that tracks the target tightly so the trajectory
is dominated by the commanded motion + the model's true dynamics). pose_legs/
arm_pose default to the spec's nominal (deep squat) when omitted. See
docs/developer/binary-parity-probe.md.

_residuals.contact_ke_kd: Deploy sets contact_ke=2500/contact_kd=100; the trainer currently uses Newton ModelBuilder defaults (does NOT apply these). spec.apply_contact_to_trainer is OFF by default so this refactor is behavior-preserving. Flip it + retrain to close the residual.
_residuals.njmax_nconmax: Deploy single-robot auto-sizes (default 256); trainer pins 128 for the 2048-env batch. Kept side-specific by necessity.
_residuals.nominal_legs: Used only in the NON-human-gait fallback. The winning recipe runs G1_GAIT_MODEL=human, where BOTH sides take the nominal from g1_human_gait.standing_pose(GaitParams) -- already a shared module. nominal_legs here must equal the deploy controller's NOMINAL_LEGS fallback.
_residuals.joint_limit_precision: The trainer's post-step joint clamp uses MJ.JOINT_LIMITS_LO/HI rounded to 3 decimals (e.g. -2.531); the winning policy was TRAINED against those exact boundaries, so they stay pinned to it. The deploy controller + backend + this spec's leg_limits() read full URDF precision (e.g. -2.5307). Gap <=4e-4 rad (sub-milliradian), only relevant at a joint pinned exactly to its limit. Unify by retraining with SPEC.leg_limits() full-precision clamp.
_residuals.deploy_link_com: FIXED (opt-in, 24eeab2d). The deploy runtime's World.add_body previously took no COM arg -> every link COM at the link origin (vs the trainer's true URDF COM; body_ipos up to 0.154 m, the dominant cause of trainer-vs-deploy trajectory drift). add_body now accepts a com (newton add_link(com=...)); WbSolid::addBody passes the link COM when OMNISIM_NEWTON_USE_LINK_COM is set (default OFF = legacy COM-at-origin, so every other Newton robot is unchanged). With the flag the golden test shows body_ipos PASS (0.0) -> full trainer/deploy MjModel parity (only representational nbody/body_mass-rollup/body_pos diffs remain). NATIVE BUILD DONE (2026-06-18): the binary was rebuilt with the COM caller (verified in-binary: OMNISIM_NEWTON_USE_LINK_COM + the embedded com param are present); the Qt5/Qt6 build blocker was fixed (src/omnisim/Makefile: user_commands TUs now get the bundled Qt6 QtNetwork). DEPLOY RE-VALIDATION (flag on): the deploy loads + steps cleanly and walks +3.93 m, but the EXISTING policy (gpu_newton_g1_walk_ft_pdoff_clamp) FALLS at ~11.7 s vs the old-COM doc baseline 33.8 s. The COM fix is proven-correct (golden-test body_ipos parity with the trainer), so this means the old long walk leaned on the deploy's INCORRECT COM -- the existing policy is not robust on the now-parity physics. A clean flag-OFF control run on the current binary could not be obtained (another sim held the GPU/log). DECISION: keep the flag OPT-IN (default off) so the existing policy + every other Newton robot are unchanged; the corrected (parity) deploy is now the RETRAIN target. Retrain on Modal (the trainer already uses true COM via add_urdf, so it is already aligned), validate the new policy with OMNISIM_NEWTON_USE_LINK_COM=1, then default it on by adding it to newton_env().
_residuals.mjcf_mass_force_clamp: FIXED (5cdc4bea). make_g1_mjcf.py now sets compiler.fusestatic=0 (the 9 fixed-joint child links were being fused away with saveinertial=0 -> ~1.28 kg lost on serialization; total was 32.85 vs 34.13 kg) and forcelimited/ctrllimited=FALSE (the live trainer+deploy leave force/ctrl unbounded PD-only; the MJCF had clamped them). The canonical MJCF now matches the trainer (P1 vs P3) on ALL structural fields incl. mass (34.1339 kg), forcerange, ctrlrange. The deploy-from-MJCF / trainer-from-MJCF switch is still GPU/rebuild-gated (a behavior change to validate), but the artifact is now faithful.
